Start

Before you install anything

read first

How to use this page

  • Each procedure is shown as an animation: a GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) file that plays by itself and starts again at the end. The number of the step is written at the top of every picture, and the instruction at the bottom.
  • To stop on a step, select Pause on this step, or select the step in the list beside the picture. Previous step and Next step move one step at a time; with the keyboard, use the left and right arrow keys while an animation has the focus. Play from step 1 starts the animation again.
  • The list beside each picture repeats the instruction of every step and adds the official link for that step.
  • Every animation and every step can be saved with the buttons Animation .gif and This step .png (PNG (Portable Network Graphics)). The tables have a button Download .csv.
  • The pictures are simplified drawings made for this course, not screenshots. The real windows have the same buttons and the same words, but different colours and details. Under each animation, a note on versions and appearance says what may differ on your computer.

Which environment do you need?

Run the readiness check of Lesson 3 first; its verdict decides your path. Table 1 gives the rule. One hypervisor is enough: do not install both on the same computer unless you have a reason, and never run virtual machines in both at the same time.

Your situationWhat to set upPart of this page
The readiness check says READY, and the host runs Windows or Linux.VirtualBox, the default choice of the course.Part 1
You already use VMware Workstation Pro, or you prefer it.VMware Workstation Pro. Create the Broadcom account today: a new profile is screened before the free downloads open.Part 2
The readiness check says NOT READY, and the cause cannot be corrected.The Learner Lab replaces the local lab. Tell the instructor before Lab 1.Part 3
Your computer is a Mac with an Apple processor.The Learner Lab. On these computers both hypervisors run only guests built for the same processor type.Part 3
Everyone, whatever the path.Accept the invitation and create the account of Part 3, animation 3A. Start a session only when a lab asks for it: a session uses your budget.Part 3

Five rules before any installation

  1. Back up your personal files. An installation adds drivers and can, in rare cases, make a system unstable (Legal Notice, section 10.3).
  2. Use the official source only. Type the address yourself. No download site, no search advertisement, no file received from another person (section 14 and Annex C).
  3. Verify the checksum of every installer before you run it. It is the integrity check of Lesson 2.
  4. Use valid licences only. Both hypervisors are free; neither needs a licence key. Never use a cracked copy (section 6.6).
  5. Install after the class, not during it. The VirtualBox installer disconnects the network for a few seconds, and the VMware installer can ask for a restart.
Part 1

Oracle VirtualBox 7.2.18

about 20 minutes

What you will do

VirtualBox is the default hypervisor of this course. You download the installer from the official page and verify it (animation 1A), you run the installation wizard (animation 1B), and you check the host-only network that will carry all lab traffic (animation 1C). You need an administrator account on your computer, about 1 gigabyte of free space for the program, and hardware virtualization enabled in the firmware settings (Microsoft: Enable virtualization on Windows).

Animation 1A – Download the installer and verify it

Animation 1A · 7 steps · about 33 seconds per loop · Windows host. Official source only.
  1. Open the official download pageType the address yourself: www.virtualbox.org, then Downloads. Read the address letter by letter. Never use a search advertisement or a download site.Official page: virtualbox.org/wiki/Downloads. Oracle lists the same files on its own download page.
  2. Read the version numberThe page names the latest release: 7.2.18 on September 17, 2026. If the page shows a higher number, take that one: it contains the latest security corrections.
  3. Select "Windows hosts"Select Windows hosts. The browser saves the file VirtualBox-7.2.18-175117-Win.exe in the folder Downloads. Mac and Linux users select the line of their own system.Other systems: the official installation chapter of the user guide covers Windows, macOS and Linux hosts.
  4. Open the list of checksumsBack on the download page, select SHA256 checksums. SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) gives the file a fixed value of 64 characters: the integrity check of Lesson 2, applied to your own download.Direct address of the list for this version: download.virtualbox.org/virtualbox/7.2.18/SHA256SUMS.
  5. Find the line of your fileThe list has one line per file. Find the line that ends with the exact name of your file, and keep this tab open.
  6. Compute the checksum of your fileOpen PowerShell in the folder Downloads and run Get-FileHash with the name of your file. Windows reads the file and displays its 64 characters.Official reference: Get-FileHash, Microsoft documentation. On macOS and Linux: shasum -a 256 file or sha256sum file.
  7. Compare the two valuesCompare the value of PowerShell with the line of the official list. Equal: the file is intact, continue. Different: delete the file, download it again, and tell the instructor if it happens twice.

Note on versions and appearance. Version shown: VirtualBox 7.2.18, build 175117, the latest release on September 17, 2026. Oracle publishes a maintenance release every few weeks: when you read this page, the number on the download page may be higher. Take the latest one. The layout of the download page changes from time to time; the link names Windows hosts and SHA256 checksums have stayed the same for years.

Animation 1B – Run the installation wizard

Animation 1B · 9 steps · about 42 seconds per loop · Windows host. About five minutes.
  1. Start the installerOpen the folder Downloads and double-click the file that you verified. Close your other programs first and save your work.
  2. Allow the installer to runWindows asks for permission. Read the line Verified publisher: it must name Oracle. Then select Yes. If the publisher is unknown, select No and delete the file.
  3. Welcome pageThe wizard opens on its welcome page. Select Next.
  4. Licence agreementRead the licence of the base package, select I accept the terms in the License Agreement, then Next. The base package is free, open-source software.
  5. Custom setup: keep the defaultsKeep every feature and the proposed folder: the application, USB (Universal Serial Bus) support, Networking (bridged and host-only) and Python support. The course needs the host-only part. Select Next.
  6. Warning: network interfacesThe installer adds network drivers and disconnects the network for a few seconds. Save your work and leave any online meeting first. Then select Yes.
  7. Missing dependencies: PythonThis page appears when Python is not installed. Python is used only to control VirtualBox from programs, and the course does not need it. Select Yes to continue.
  8. Ready to installSelect Install. If Windows asks whether to install device software from Oracle, select Install again. The copy takes one or two minutes.The user guide adds: if Windows displays a warning about drivers, select Continue or Install, otherwise VirtualBox may not work after the installation.
  9. FinishKeep Start Oracle VirtualBox after installation ticked and select Finish. The program is now in the Start menu, in the group Oracle VirtualBox.

Note on versions and appearance. The page names and their order follow the Windows installer of the 7.2 series. A later release can add, remove or rename a page. When the wizard and this drawing differ, follow the wizard and the official installation chapter. The network warning of step 6 is real: install after the class, not during an online session.

Animation 1C – First start and the host-only network

Animation 1C · 7 steps · about 33 seconds per loop · The private network that carries all lab traffic.
  1. Check the installed versionVirtualBox Manager opens. Select Help, then About VirtualBox, and read the version: 7.2.18 r175117. Write it in your lab notes.
  2. Open the network toolSelect Network in the bar on the left. In older releases: menu File, Tools, Network Manager.
  3. Open the tab "Host-only Networks"Select the tab Host-only Networks. On Windows, the installer has usually created one adapter already. If the list is empty, select Create.
  4. Read the address of the adapterSelect the adapter and open Properties, tab Adapter. The host uses 192.168.56.1 with the mask 255.255.255.0: the range 192.168.56.0/24 of Lesson 3.
  5. Check the address serverTab DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) Server: keep Enable Server ticked. This small service gives an address of the range to each lab machine. Select Apply if you changed a value.
  6. Leave the Extension Pack asideThe tool Extensions installs the Extension Pack. This course does not need it, and its licence is free only for personal use and evaluation. Install nothing here.Licence text: VirtualBox Personal Use and Evaluation License.
  7. Ready for Lab 2VirtualBox is ready. The guide of each lab tells you which virtual machines to create and attaches them to this host-only network. Run the readiness check again: the last line must now pass.

Note on versions and appearance. Release 7.2 placed the tools Home, Machines, Extensions, Media, Network, Cloud, Activities in a vertical bar on the left of the window. In releases 7.0 and 7.1 the same screen is reached by the menu File, Tools, Network Manager. The default range 192.168.56.0/24 has been the same for many years, but read your own values: another range works equally well, as long as you write it in your lab notes.

Mac and Linux hosts

The animations show a Windows host, the most common case in the group. On a Mac with an Intel processor, open the downloaded disk image and run the installer package; macOS then asks you to allow the system software of Oracle in the privacy and security settings. On Linux, install the package made for your distribution; the installer builds kernel modules, so the kernel headers must be present. The official installation chapter of the user guide gives the exact steps for each system. On a Mac with an Apple processor, see Table 1.

Part 2

VMware Workstation Pro 26H1u1

about 30 minutes, plus the account

What you will do

VMware Workstation Pro is the alternative hypervisor for Windows and Linux hosts. Broadcom has made it free for personal, educational and commercial use, and it asks for no licence key. The download requires a free account on the Broadcom support portal. You create the account and download the installer (animation 2A), you run the installation wizard (animation 2B), and you check the host-only network (animation 2C).

Plan ahead

The official article of Broadcom states that a new profile is screened by its export compliance team before the free downloads open, and that this screening can take a long time. Create the account today with accurate data. If the downloads are not open when Lab 1 starts, use VirtualBox.

Animation 2A – Broadcom account and download

Animation 2A · 9 steps · about 42 seconds per loop · Free product; the download requires a free account.
  1. Open the Broadcom support portalType the address yourself: support.broadcom.com. Select Register if you have no account, or Login if you have one.Official article: Download Desktop Hypervisor (Workstation and Fusion) Products. Registration: Register for an account and the registration form.
  2. Create the account with accurate dataEnter your e-mail address, type the verification code that Broadcom sends you, then complete the profile with your real name, address and country. Invented data fails the screening.
  3. Plan for the screening delayBroadcom screens each new profile for export compliance before the free downloads open. The official article says that this can take a long time. Register today, and install VirtualBox meanwhile.
  4. Choose the divisionAfter the login, open the list at the top of the portal and choose VMware Cloud Foundation. Workstation Pro belongs to that division.
  5. Open "My Downloads"In the menu on the left, select My Downloads.
  6. Open the free downloadsSelect the sentence Free Software Downloads available HERE.
  7. Find VMware Workstation ProType Workstation in the search field, select Show Results, then select VMware Workstation Pro.
  8. Choose the release and downloadOpen VMware Workstation Pro for Windows, choose the latest release, 26H1u1, tick I agree to the Terms and Conditions, then select the download symbol.Release notes of this version: VMware Workstation Pro 26H1u1 Release Notes. If the download does not start: Unable to download VMware Workstation Pro.
  9. Verify the fileThe portal lists the checksums of the file. Compute the SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) value of your copy with Get-FileHash, as for VirtualBox, and compare. Different values: delete the file and download it again.

Note on versions and appearance. Version shown: VMware Workstation Pro 26H1u1, build 25688693, released on September 3, 2026 and the latest on September 17, 2026. The steps follow the official Broadcom article 368734. Broadcom reorganizes its portal often: a menu can move, and a label can change. Two facts from that article matter for your planning: the account data must be accurate, and a new profile is screened by the export compliance team before the free downloads open, which can take time. Register today, and keep VirtualBox as your first choice.

Animation 2B – Run the installation wizard

Animation 2B · 9 steps · about 42 seconds per loop · Windows host. About ten minutes; a restart may be needed.
  1. Start the installerSign in to Windows with an administrator account. Double-click the file that you verified. Windows asks for permission: the publisher line must name VMware or Broadcom. Select Yes.
  2. Welcome pageThe wizard opens. Select Next.
  3. Licence agreementRead the agreement, tick I accept the terms in the License Agreement, then select Next. The product is free for personal, educational and commercial use.
  4. Only if Windows runs its own hypervisorThis page appears when a Windows feature such as Hyper-V is active. Tick Install Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHP (Windows Hypervisor Platform)) automatically, then Next. The virtual machines work, a little more slowly.
  5. Custom setup: keep the folderKeep the proposed folder. Leave Enhanced Keyboard Driver unticked: the course does not need it, and it forces a restart. Select Next.
  6. User experience settingsKeep Check for product updates on startup: security corrections arrive several times a year. The second box sends usage data to the publisher; tick it or not, as you prefer. Select Next.
  7. ShortcutsKeep the two shortcuts, Desktop and Start Menu Programs Folder, and select Next.
  8. Install, then finishSelect Install. At the end, select Finish. If the wizard asks for a restart, save your work and restart now.
  9. Check the installed versionStart the program. It asks for no licence key. Select Help, then About VMware Workstation, and write the version in your lab notes: 26H1u1, build 25688693.

Note on versions and appearance. The official procedure is short: sign in as an administrator, double-click the installer, follow the prompts, restart if asked. The page names drawn here follow the wizard of recent releases; release 26H1u1 can show them in another order or with other words. Since release 26H1 the program is a 64-bit application and proposes the folder C:\Program Files\VMware\VMware Workstation. No licence key is requested. If the wizard and this drawing differ, follow the wizard and the official installation page.

Animation 2C – The host-only network

Animation 2C · 6 steps · about 29 seconds per loop · Where the private lab network is set.
  1. Open the Virtual Network EditorIn VMware Workstation, select Edit, then Virtual Network Editor.
  2. Unlock the settingsThe values are read-only at first. Select Change Settings and answer Yes to the permission window of Windows.
  3. Select VMnet1, the host-only networkSelect the line VMnet1. Its type is Host-only: the lab machines reach one another and the host, and nothing else.
  4. Check the two boxes and read the subnetKeep Connect a host virtual adapter to this network and Use local DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) service ticked. Read the subnet address and write it in your lab notes. Change it only if a lab guide asks for a precise range.
  5. Know the two other networksVMnet0 is bridged: not used in this course. VMnet8 uses NAT (Network Address Translation): connect it only for the time of an update, then disconnect it. This is the rule of Lesson 3.
  6. Close with OKSelect OK. VMware Workstation Pro is ready: the guide of each lab attaches the virtual machines to VMnet1.

Note on versions and appearance. The Virtual Network Editor exists on Windows hosts; on Linux hosts the same tool is started with the command vmware-netcfg. The three network names have been stable for many years: VMnet0 is bridged, VMnet1 is host-only, VMnet8 uses network address translation. The subnet addresses in the drawing are examples: VMware chooses them at random during the installation, so yours will differ.

Linux and Mac hosts

On a Linux host, the download is a file with the extension .bundle: make it executable and run it as an administrator; the parent page Installing Workstation Pro links to the procedure. On a Mac, the equivalent product is VMware Fusion Pro, downloaded from the same portal in the same way.

Part 3

The Learner Lab of AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy

about 15 minutes

What you will do

The Learner Lab gives each student a temporary cloud account with a budget of credits. It replaces the local lab when a computer cannot run virtual machines, and it shows how cloud resources are monitored. Nothing is installed on your computer: you need the invitation of the instructor and a web browser. You accept the invitation and create the account (animation 3A), you start a session and open the console (animation 3B), and you learn the four habits that protect your budget and your work (animation 3C). Your course has the number 170913: awsacademy.instructure.com/courses/170913.

Animation 3A – Accept the invitation and create the account

Animation 3A · 7 steps · about 33 seconds per loop · You need the invitation that the instructor sends by e-mail.
  1. Find the invitationThe instructor adds your College e-mail address to the course. You receive a message titled Course Invitation. Look in the junk folder too. Select Get Started.
  2. Create the accountNew to AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy: select Create My Account. If you already have an account on this platform, select I Have a Canvas Account and sign in.
  3. Choose a password and registerChoose a long password that you use nowhere else, select your time zone, accept the acceptable use policy, then select Register.
  4. Sign in the next timesLater, type the address yourself: awsacademy.instructure.com. Sign in with the same e-mail address and password. Keep this address in your bookmarks.Portal: awsacademy.instructure.com. Your course: course 170913.
  5. Open the course from the dashboardThe Dashboard shows one tile per course. If a banner asks you to accept the invitation, select Accept. Then select the tile AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy Learner Lab.
  6. Open the list "Modules"Inside the course, select Modules in the menu of the course. The list contains the guide, the rules and the lab itself.
  7. Read the Student Guide firstOpen the Student Guide and read it before you start the lab. If the list contains a module on rules and security with a short test, complete it: some courses require it.General presentation of the program: AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy.

Note on versions and appearance. The Learner Lab is delivered through a learning platform of the company Instructure, named Canvas, at the address awsacademy.instructure.com, and the lab itself runs in a tool of the company Vocareum. Both change their screens without notice, so the position and the name of a button may differ from this drawing. The official Student Guide is the first item in the list Modules of your course: it is the reference when a screen differs. Your course has the number 170913.

Animation 3B – Start a session and open the console

Animation 3B · 8 steps · about 38 seconds per loop · From the list Modules to the management console.
  1. Launch the Learner LabIn Modules, select the item that launches the lab. Its name is Launch AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy Learner Lab or simply Learner Lab, depending on the version of the course.
  2. Accept the terms of the lab toolThe first time, the lab tool displays its terms and conditions. Read them, scroll to the end and select I Agree.
  3. Look at the lab pageThe dot beside AWS (Amazon Web Services) is red: no session is running. The top line shows your budget and the timer. On the right, Readme lists the permitted services and regions: read it once.
  4. Select "Start Lab"Select Start Lab. The first start creates your temporary account and takes several minutes. The dot turns yellow while the environment is prepared.
  5. Wait for the green dotWhen the dot is green, the session is ready, and the timer counts down from 4 hours. Select Start Lab again at any time to set the timer back to 4 hours.
  6. Open the consoleSelect the word AWS (Amazon Web Services) beside the green dot. The AWS (Amazon Web Services) Management Console opens in a new tab. If nothing happens, allow pop-up windows for this site in your browser.
  7. Check the regionIn the console, read the region at the top right: United States (N. Virginia), us-east-1. The Learner Lab permits only us-east-1 and us-west-2. An action in another region is refused.
  8. Return to the lab tabKeep both tabs open. You work in the console tab, and you control the session in the lab tab: budget, timer, key file and the button End Lab.

Note on versions and appearance. The steps follow the official Student Guide of the Learner Lab. The lab page is provided by Vocareum and the console by Amazon Web Services; both are redesigned regularly, and the console in particular changes its colours and menus several times a year. What stays stable: the buttons Start Lab, End Lab, AWS (Amazon Web Services) Details, Readme and Reset, the coloured dot beside the word AWS (Amazon Web Services), the budget line and the session timer.

Animation 3C – Key file, budget, timer and end of session

Animation 3C · 7 steps · about 33 seconds per loop · The four habits that protect your budget and your work.
  1. Download the key fileSelect AWS (Amazon Web Services) Details, then Download PEM (Privacy-Enhanced Mail). The file labsuser.pem is the private key for SSH (Secure Shell) connections to your virtual servers. Users of the program PuTTY take Download PPK (PuTTY Private Key).Official background: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) key pairs.
  2. Protect the key fileStore labsuser.pem in a folder that only you can read. Never send it, never post it, never put it in a submission. A private key is a confidentiality asset, as in Lesson 2.
  3. Read the budget lineThe top line shows what you have used. The figure comes from the billing service and can be up to 8 hours late: what you start now appears later. Stop or delete what you do not use.
  4. Know what continues to costAt the end of a session, running EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) instances are stopped and start again with the next session. Some other resources, for example NAT (Network Address Translation) gateways and database services, continue to cost: delete them when the exercise ends.
  5. Do not select "Reset"Reset erases every resource of your account and cannot be undone: all work is lost, and the budget already used is not given back. Select it only if the instructor tells you to.
  6. End the sessionWhen you stop working, select End Lab and confirm with Yes. The dot turns red. Your work is kept for the next session. Without this step the session ends alone after 4 hours.
  7. If the budget runs lowIf the budget is entirely spent, the account is closed and the work is lost. Write to the instructor as soon as the used amount passes one half, and before you start anything that runs for days.

Note on versions and appearance. The rules of this animation come from the official Student Guide: the budget display can be late by up to 8 hours; the button Reset erases all your work; at the end of a session the running virtual servers are stopped and start again with the next session; some other resources continue to cost money outside a session; a spent budget closes the account, and the work is lost. The amount of the budget depends on the version of the Learner Lab and is written on your own lab page; older official guides mention 100 United States dollars.

Rules of the course for the Learner Lab

  1. Fictional data only. No real name, no real password and no real document goes into the cloud account (Legal Notice, section 6.7).
  2. The terms of the provider apply in addition to the rules of the course, and you alone answer for what you leave running (section 6.4).
  3. Stay in the permitted region and use only the services that a lab guide names.
  4. End the session when you stop working, and delete what the exercise no longer needs.
  5. Never share the key file labsuser.pem, and never place it in a submission (section 17.2).
Help

If something does not work

when needed

Common problems and what to do

What you seeLikely causeWhat to do
The VirtualBox installer stops and asks for the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable.A set of Microsoft program files is missing on this computer.Install the latest supported package from the official page of Microsoft, then start the VirtualBox installer again.
The network or the online meeting stops for a few seconds during the installation of VirtualBox.The installer adds network drivers. It announced this on the page Warning: Network Interfaces.Wait; the connection returns by itself. Install after the class.
A 64-bit virtual machine does not start, and the message names hardware virtualization.The processor feature is switched off in the firmware settings.Enable it: Enable virtualization on Windows. Then run the readiness check again.
The virtual machines are slow. The readiness report says Windows hypervisor active = True.Windows runs its own hypervisor for some of its security features, and the two hypervisors share the processor.Accept the lower speed, and give each virtual machine fewer processors. Do not switch off security features of Windows on your own; ask the instructor first.
The Broadcom portal shows no free downloads.The new profile is still being screened, or the division VMware Cloud Foundation is not selected.Select the division, then wait for the approval. Meanwhile use VirtualBox. Official article: download steps.
No invitation from AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy in your mailbox.The message is in the junk folder, or the address was typed with an error.Search the mailbox for the words Course Invitation. Then write to the instructor by MIO (Messagerie interne Omnivox, the internal messaging of the College) with your exact College e-mail address.
You select the word beside the green dot and no console opens.The browser blocks pop-up windows.Allow pop-up windows for the site of the lab in the settings of the browser, then select the word again.
The dot stays yellow for more than 15 minutes.The start of the session did not complete.Select End Lab, wait one minute, then Start Lab. If it happens again, tell the instructor.
The console answers that you are not authorized.The region or the service is outside the limits of the Learner Lab.Return to the region us-east-1 and read the list of permitted services in Readme.
